subject: Issue while ploting a recordPlot object in a Shiny APp

messages.author: 8899033a1963ffa1
messages.subject: Issue while ploting a recordPlot object in a Shiny APp
parts:
Hi,

I would like to save some graphs (classical plots, not ggplot2) recorded using recordPlot and plot them again during another session (using replayPlot).
The use of recordPlot / replayPlot works well in Shiny (see below), but I have an error (Error in : NULL value passed as symbol address) when I save / reload the recordPlot object.
Any clue?

Here is a code that shows the issue.

library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
   sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(
         sliderInput("bins","Number of bins:", min = 1, max = 50, value = 30)
      ),
      # Show the plots and the "stored" graph
      mainPanel(
        plotOutput("distPlot"),
        plotOutput("distPlotS"),
        verbatimTextOutput("RecordedPlot")
      )
   )
)
server <- function(input, output) {
  
   distPlot <- reactive({
     x    <- faithful[, 2]
     bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = input$bins + 1)
     hist(x, breaks = bins, col = 'darkgray', border = 'white')
     recordPlot()    
   })
   #I save the graph, and reload it
   saveload <- reactive({
     res <- distPlot()
     save(res,file="tmp")
     rm("res")
     load("tmp")
     return(res)
   })
   output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
     # generate plot recorded in the session : OK
     replayPlot(distPlot())
   })
   output$distPlotS <- renderPlot({
     # generate plot saved/loaded: not OK
     replayPlot(saveload())
   })
   #The object is OK
   output$RecordedPlot <- renderPrint(unclass(saveload()))
}

# Run the application
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.subject: Re: Issue while ploting a recordPlot object in a Shiny APp
parts:
Update: I found an interesting webpage explaining why there is a bug and suggesting that this should not happen for version R>3.3.0 (I use R>3.4.1!).
I did some tries using the load, the attach and the reloadPkgs options from recordPlot and replayPlot, without success.

Eventually, following the  webpage, I found a(n awful) solution to reconnect the pointers to the memory addresses. I modify my recorded recordPlot object like this.

x <- readRDS("tmp")

for(i in 1:length(x[[1]])){
  dllName <- x[[1]][[i]][[2]][[1]][["package"]][["name"]]
  if(is.null(dllName)) 
    dllName <- x[[1]][[i]][[2]][[1]][["dll"]][["name"]]  
  pkgDLL <- getLoadedDLLs()[[dllName]]
  x[[1]][[i]][[2]][[1]] <- getNativeSymbolInfo(x[[1]][[i]][[2]][[1]]$name, PACKAGE=pkgDLL)
}

It works. The complete Shiny app is as following

library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
   sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(
         sliderInput("bins","Number of bins:", min = 1, max = 50, value = 30)
      ),
      # Show the plots and the "stored" graph 
      mainPanel(
        plotOutput("distPlot"),
        plotOutput("distPlotS"),
        verbatimTextOutput("RecordedPlot")
      )
   )
)
server <- function(input, output) {
   
   distPlot <- reactive({
     x    <- faithful[, 2] 
     bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = input$bins + 1)
# draw the histogram with the specified number of bins

hist(x, breaks = bins, col = 'darkgray', border = 'white')
     recordPlot()
   })
   #I save the graph, and reload it
   saveload <- reactive({
     res <- distPlot()

saveRDS(res, file="tmp")
     rm("res")
     res <- readRDS("tmp")

return(res)
   })
   output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
     # generate plot recorded in the session : OK
     replayPlot(distPlot())
   })
   output$distPlotS <- renderPlot({

# generate plot saved/loaded: now OK
     x <- saveload()
     for(i in 1:length(x[[1]])){
       dllName <- x[[1]][[i]][[2]][[1]][["package"]][["name"]]
       if(is.null(dllName)) 
         dllName <- x[[1]][[i]][[2]][[1]][["dll"]][["name"]]  
       pkgDLL <- getLoadedDLLs()[[dllName]]
       x[[1]][[i]][[2]][[1]] <- getNativeSymbolInfo(x[[1]][[i]][[2]][[1]]$name, PACKAGE=pkgDLL)
     }
     replayPlot(x,reloadPkgs=TRUE)
   })
   output$RecordedPlotO <- renderPrint(unclass(distPlot()))

output$RecordedPlot <- renderPrint(unclass(saveload()))
}

# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
